start_notice: A historical mission with fictional return decisions and alternate outcomes.

nodes.title: Mission briefing
nodes.text: Your crew will attempt docking with Agena. Choose up to two supplemental ground rehearsals. The crew's training and the mission rules are already in place. You are deciding which handoffs this room will practice together.

nodes.prompt: Choose up to two supplemental ground rehearsals.
nodes.text: Each rehearsal is a performed ground exercise. It records what this room practiced together; it does not change the crew's training, the radio coverage, the ships, or the spacecraft.

options.intent: Rehearse sender, receipt and acknowledgement handoffs.
options.uncertainty: Supports either route; does not improve radio coverage.
Helps a stretched recovery; does not put ships closer.

options.intent: Rehearse routing an uncertain reserve warning.
options.uncertainty: Helps the extra-orbit handoff; does not increase reserve.

lines.speaker: g8-capcom
lines.text: Docking is confirmed. We'll carry that report into the next contact.

nodes.title: Loss of contact
nodes.text: The scheduled contact has ended. There is no new spacecraft report.

nodes.title: A silent loop is not a diagnosis.

lines.speaker: g8-capcom
lines.text: We have the last report. We do not have the next one.
The handoff board has a blank acknowledgement field for the next report.

answer.speaker: g8-capcom
answer.text: Docking was reported. Current attitude and crew actions are not visible to us here.

lines.speaker: g8-capcom
lines.text: An emergency report has reached the tracking ship. The crew are dealing with the tumble onboard.

lines.speaker: g8-systems
lines.text: They've regained control using RCS. End the remaining objectives. Now we decide how to bring them home.

lines.speaker: g8-systems
lines.text: The room has rehearsed separating a warning from a diagnosis. We still do not have the complete diagnosis.

nodes.title: Return planning
nodes.prompt: Which danger are you willing to carry?

lines.speaker: g8-flight-dynamics
lines.text: Two return opportunities in this plan. The first gets them down sooner. The second puts the recovery force closer. We cannot have both.

lines.speaker: g8-systems
lines.text: Get them off the spacecraft. Stable is what they're doing now. It isn't a promise about another orbit.

lines.speaker: g8-recovery
lines.text: And the ocean is not a safe room. Give me the later opportunity and I can have the recovery force waiting closer to them.

questions.text: What does the earlier return cost them?

answer.speaker: g8-recovery
answer.text: A long wait for pickup. Air support helps, but it cannot turn a distant ship into a nearby one. A clean handoff can shorten the last part.

questions.text: What does another orbit cost them?

answer.speaker: g8-systems
answer.text: More exposure on a damaged spacecraft and less room for a confused entry handoff. Rehearsal helps us handle the warning. It does not replenish the reserve.

options.intent: Bring them down at the earlier opportunity.
options.attraction: Ends exposure aboard the damaged spacecraft sooner. Backs Mara's priority.
options.cost: Accept a prolonged wait at sea and the crew's increasing exhaustion. Elias must execute with sparse surface coverage.
options.unavailable_reason: The contingency return has not been directed.

options.intent: Take the later opportunity, one additional modeled orbit.
options.attraction: Concentrates recovery support near pickup and avoids the earlier route's long sea wait. Backs Elias's priority.
options.cost: Keep the crew aboard as control reserve becomes critical. Mara must execute a more demanding warning/entry handoff.
options.unavailable_reason: The contingency return has not been directed.

resolutions.text: Final pickup instruction requires an ownership clarification and an acknowledgement retry.

lines.speaker: g8-capcom
lines.text: Splashdown confirmed. Both crew members responding.

lines.speaker: g8-recovery
lines.text: They're down. My part is not over.

lines.speaker: g8-systems
lines.text: Reserve warning. This is the margin we spent to reach their recovery force.

resolutions.text: The pickup approach is delayed by the two ground handoff corrections. The crew are badly exhausted by the time the retrieval team reaches them; both need help transferring aboard.
One ground handoff needs correction before pickup. The crew are exhausted after the sea wait, but the retrieval team completes the transfer.
The rehearsed handoffs avoid an additional pickup delay. The sea wait still leaves the crew worn down; the retrieval team brings both aboard.
The reserve warning and its acknowledgement need two ground handoff corrections. Entry coordination becomes a scramble. The crew complete entry and reach the closer recovery force visibly spent.
One ground handoff needs correction under the reserve warning. The room completes the entry handoff under strain. The crew reach the closer recovery force tired but responsive.

The reserve warning and protective recommendation pass through the rehearsed handoffs without rework. Reserve remains critical through the modeled entry sequence. The crew reach the closer recovery force tired but responsive.

nodes.title: Who carries the blame?
nodes.header_label: Historical disagreement; fictional player stance and relationship effects.
nodes.text: They came home. Now the argument moves from the flight room to the astronaut office. Some call the crew's judgment into question. Others ask what the ground failed to prepare for. Your position will tell the crews whether this room stands behind them when the checklist runs out.

nodes.title: Who carries the blame?
nodes.header_label: Historical disagreement; fictional player stance and relationship effects.

options.intent: Side with Cunningham and Stafford; blame the crew's handling of the emergency.
options.statement: I agree with the criticism. Armstrong and Scott's handling of the emergency deserves the blame.
options.attraction: Align with the critics and keep the director's ground organization out of the center of his own criticism. Fictional support from Cunningham and Stafford strengthens.
options.cost: Armstrong and Scott lose trust in Glen; the director's endorsement deepens division within the corps.
options.uncertainty: This stance does not overturn the reported analysis clearing the crew.
options.unavailable_reason: Requires the recovered crew, the recorded relationship response, one baseline lesson, the post-flight context, and no prior stance.

effects.label: Glen sided with the crew's critics

options.intent: Take the historically grounded Kranz position: the ground lacked docked-flight contingencies.
options.subtitle: Historically grounded response
options.statement: The failure we own is the lack of ground contingency procedures for the docked phase. We will correct that. I will not blame Armstrong and Scott for bringing the spacecraft home.
options.attraction: Back the crew and direct the program toward a concrete contingency-procedure response.
options.cost: Glen openly accepts responsibility for a failure in the ground organization.
options.uncertainty: Historical disagreement among astronauts is not magically erased; no invented funding penalty is attached.
options.unavailable_reason: Requires the recovered crew, the recorded relationship response, one baseline lesson, the post-flight context, and no prior stance.

effects.label: Glen took responsibility for the ground contingency gap

debrief.text: Docking was achieved. The remaining objectives were terminated. Both crew members were recovered alive.
You chose to end spacecraft exposure sooner and accepted a prolonged sea recovery.
You chose another modeled orbit to improve pickup coverage. The crew carried the control-reserve warning through that return.
The recovery rehearsal was used in the pickup handoff. It avoided an ownership correction; it did not shorten the ship's transit.
The systems rehearsal was used to route the reserve warning. It avoided a repeated ground assessment; it did not replenish the reserve.
The contact rehearsal was used to confirm the instruction's receipt. It avoided an acknowledgement retry during the return.
The logged handoff corrections affected the return you ordered. Their effects are recorded in the crew-condition and entry/pickup reports.
Elias's response is recorded above. The next mission must include a recovery rehearsal; you will choose its companion exercise.
Mara's response is recorded above. The next mission must include a systems-warning rehearsal; you will choose its companion exercise.
You carried report provenance into the procedures binder.
You carried recovery cross-checking into the procedures binder.

You endorsed the criticism of Armstrong and Scott. The recorded fictional response strengthened your support among the critics, reduced both crew members' trust in you, and deepened division in the astronaut corps.

You took responsibility for the ground contingency gap. The recorded fictional response strengthened the crew's trust in you and commissioned docked-flight contingency work. This follows the direction of Kranz's criticism as reported in the historical source.
